title: Unshifted coefficient-unit and Tate-line multiplication in a tower
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $S$. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for each finite extension $L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizer $\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], put $R_L=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,S}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $U_L=R_L[0]$. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].
Let $L_0\subseteq L_1\subseteq L_2$ be finite coefficient extensions, allowing repeated fields, let $m\ge0$, and put $J_i=\mathcal O_{L_i}(m)$ and $V_i=U_{L_i}(m)$. Write $C_{ji}=-\otimes^L_{R_{L_i}}R_{L_j}$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $\iota_{ji}:R_{L_i}\to R_{L_j}$ for inclusion, and $\alpha:C_{21}C_{10}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{20}$ for ordinary derived tensor associativity, identified with completed extensions by the specified $\chi$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Define $u_{ji}:C_{ji}U_{L_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{L_j}$ by the canonical K-flat resolving comparison followed by coefficient multiplication $x\otimes b\mapsto\iota_{ji}(x)b$. Let $\beta_{ji}$ be the specified twist/scalar comparison [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar], in ordinary coordinates via $\chi$, and put $w_{ji}=u_{ji}(m)\circ\beta_{ji,U_{L_i}}:C_{ji}V_i\xrightarrow{\sim}V_j$. Let $b_{ji}:J_i\otimes_{R_{L_i}}R_{L_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j$ be the canonical twist-line map [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change].
The maps $u_{ji}$ and $w_{ji}$ are represented on the degree-zero models by
$$x\otimes b\longmapsto\iota_{ji}(x)b,\qquad (x\otimes z)\otimes b\longmapsto\iota_{ji}(x)b\,b_{ji}(z\otimes1),$$
and the inverse coefficient-unit map is $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. They satisfy
$$u_{20}\circ\alpha_{U_{L_0}}=u_{21}\circ C_{21}(u_{10}),\qquad w_{20}\circ\alpha_{V_0}=w_{21}\circ C_{21}(w_{10}).$$
On $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)$ both unit paths have value $\iota_{20}(x)\iota_{21}(b)c$. On $(((x\otimes z)\otimes b)\otimes c)$ the direct line path has value $\iota_{20}(x)\iota_{21}(b)c\,b_{20}(z\otimes1)$ and the successive path has value $\iota_{20}(x)\iota_{21}(b)c\,b_{21}(b_{10}(z\otimes1)\otimes1)$; these expressions define equal sheaf morphisms and equal derived morphisms. For $j=i$, $u_{ii}$ is the tensor multiplication unitor and $w_{ii}$ is the line multiplication unitor. Under $\chi$, these identity comparisons use the natural derived-completeness map, not a strict identification of the completed identity extension with the identity functor. All assertions include $m=0$ and repeated fields.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to coefficient transport, sk-thm-purity-transport Step 3; Old Steps 4-5 and identity part of Step 7: specified coefficient multiplication and unshifted Tate-line tower maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-tate-unit-flat-model-domains] at each $L_i$, with the given $m$ and $n=0$. It supplies flat-term K-flat degree-zero models $R_i[0]$ and $(R_i\otimes_{R_i}J_i)[0]$ for $U_i,V_i$, their completeness and integral constructible membership, and the specified $\chi$. Thus the domain condition for $\beta_{ji,U_i}$ is met. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], their identity resolutions compute $C_{ji}$; by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], the resulting scalar-extended models are again flat-term K-flat, so a second extension is computed on the same models. No replacement between the two extensions changes their degree-zero tensor formulas.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); application to the existing Tate-unit models

proof.text: On sections the balanced map $R_i\times R_j\to R_j$, $(x,b)\mapsto\iota_{ji}(x)b$, defines a sheaf map $\mu_{ji}:R_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to R_j$ by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. Its inverse is $b\mapsto1\otimes b$: multiplication gives $b$ in one direction, and in the other $1\otimes\iota_{ji}(x)b=x\otimes b$ by the balancing relation. The formulas commute with restrictions. Step 1 and the definition of $u_{ji}$ therefore identify $u_{ji}$ with $\mu_{ji}[0]$ through the specified resolving comparison. This proves the asserted unit formula and its inverse, without choosing a basis.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), bilinear universal property following Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor)

proof.text: Use the actual termwise comparison in [lem-weil-integral-twist-derived-scalar] with the identity resolution of $U_i$ from step 1. In ordinary coordinates it sends $(x\otimes z)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes b)\otimes b_{ji}(z\otimes1)$. Tensoring the multiplication from step 2 with $J_j$ consequently sends this to $\iota_{ji}(x)b\,b_{ji}(z\otimes1)$. This is exactly $u_{ji}(m)\circ\beta_{ji,U_i}=w_{ji}$. The cited comparison is a chain isomorphism conjugated by the specified $\chi$, so this computation refers to the stated comparison, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the same objects.

source.place: Coefficient transport auxiliary: specified twist/scalar map; supporting blueprint prop-weil-twist-preserves, final paragraph

proof.text: For either degree-zero model $M=R_0$ or $M=R_0\otimes_{R_0}J_0$, the ordinary scalar associator is $((a\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto a\otimes\iota_{21}(b)c$. Its inverse is $a\otimes c\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes c$. These are balanced over $R_0$ and $R_1$; their two composites are identities since $(a\otimes1)\otimes\iota_{21}(b)c=(a\otimes b)\otimes c$. Applying [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] successively makes these formulas sheaf maps and proves their equalities on sheaf tensors. By step 1 their degree-zero chain maps represent the specified ordinary derived $\alpha$, with no total-complex signs.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), associativity and scalar-extension formulas, with bilinear universal property after Tag 0GMW

proof.text: Using steps 2 and 4, the direct unit path sends $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)$ to $\iota_{20}(x)\iota_{21}(b)c$. The successive unit path sends it to $\iota_{21}(\iota_{10}(x)b)c$, the same expression because the coefficient inclusions compose and preserve multiplication. These are equal sheaf maps by the iterated bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. Applying the derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to this equality of the representing degree-zero chain maps gives $u_{20}\alpha_{U_0}=u_{21}C_{21}(u_{10})$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product): balanced multiplication and sheaf tensor universal property

proof.text: By steps 3 and 4, the direct line path on $(((x\otimes z)\otimes b)\otimes c)$ has value $\iota_{20}(x)\iota_{21}(b)c\,b_{20}(z\otimes1)$. The successive path has value $\iota_{20}(x)\iota_{21}(b)c\,b_{21}(b_{10}(z\otimes1)\otimes1)$: in the second application of step 3, the scalar $\iota_{10}(x)b$ passes through $\iota_{21}$. The tower clause of [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change] says precisely that the two remaining line factors agree. Repeated application of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] gives equality of the sheaf maps, and hence equality of their degree-zero chain maps and their images under derived localization. This proves $w_{20}\alpha_{V_0}=w_{21}C_{21}(w_{10})$ with the two requested representative formulas.

source.place: Coefficient transport auxiliary: ordinary line multiplication in a tower; supporting prop-weil-twist-preserves, integral coefficient paragraph

proof.text: For the identity inclusion, step 2 is $x\otimes b\mapsto xb$, the multiplication unitor. For $m\geq0$, [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change] defines $b_{ii}$ by tensor associativity on the tensor powers (the coefficient unit for $m=0$); for the identity ring map this is $z\otimes b\mapsto bz$. Step 3 therefore becomes $(x\otimes z)\otimes b\mapsto xb z$, the line multiplication unitor. The tower computations used neither strict inclusion nor $m>0$, so they include repeated fields and $m=0$; they also hold on the empty site. Finally [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] explicitly identifies $\chi_{L_i/L_i,K}$, after the ordinary multiplication unitor, with the natural map from $K$ to its derived completion. Thus the completed identity comparison is this map, as asserted, and was never treated as a strict identity functor.
